newsitem.title: USA: BGE, Goldman Sachs in power marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: BGE, Goldman Sachs in power marketing pact.

text.p: Baltimore Gas and Electric Co on Tuesday teamed up with Goldman Sachs to form a power marketing subsidiary to compete in the national wholesale electric industry, the companies said.

The nation's first gas utility, BGE in an exclusive pact with Goldman Sachs Power is seeking to expand its energy business beyond the Baltimore-Washington corridor and prepare for retail competition in a deregulated U.S. energy industry, BGE executives said.

BGE plans to make a $100 million capital investment in its power marketing subsidiary, Constellation Power Source, which will be based in Baltimore and staffed by 50 people from both companies, executives said.
"We'll be in the top ten in electrics," BGE Chairman Christian Poindexter said. "I think we would be prepared with this new company to be (competing) across the country."

BGE is merging with neighboring electric utility Potomac Electric Power Co in a deal that will create one of the nation's ten largest utilities with more than $15 billion in assets, 1.8 million electric and 550,000 gas customers.

More than 300 companies have sought power marketing certificates, but only 73 were active last year and ten controlled nearly 75 percent of the wholesale electric market, according to federal regulators.
The rival power marketers are jockeying for market share in a soon-to-be deregulated retail electric and natural gas market valued at more than $305 billion a year.

Constellation Power plans to file for a power marketing certificate with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission next week. Goldman Sachs has held a FERC certificate for more than a year, but has been inactive in the physical market, executives said.
BGE has stakes in 25 independent U.S. power projects with a combined capacity of nearly 900 megawatts in high-cost states like California, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Hawaii.

Its Constellation Power unit will initially focus on the wholesale market, targeting large commercial and industrial customers. The company has no plans to compete for residential customers outside its service territory in the Baltimore- Washington corridor, said Charles Shivery, Constellation Power's newly named chief executive officer.
